prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Full SCENE STATE SHEET for a physical Mars expedition game. Match the supplied realistic painterly cream-and-teal machinery, ochre landscape, restrained cobalt science equipment, mustard rover fittings. Locally made parts are simple cut straight steel and bolted joints, never elaborate molded industrial machinery. Factory precision parts are imported. No people, text, numerals, labels, captions, borders, arrows, diagrams or UI. Each panel repeats EXACTLY the same camera, framing, object positions, light, room/landscape and perspective, changing ONLY the specified state. Every recurring object is the same actual object. Frame the full installation in the upper two thirds; lower third is quiet natural floor or ground for the movable inventory. No loose decorative objects. Whole scenes will be cropped into registered fixed targets; keep independent working regions clearly separated. Square panels, not portrait strips.
Layout: 3 columns by 1 rows of equal SQUARE scenes. Reading order left to right then next row. Same GROWN three-zone farm as FINAL panel of reference 1, with extended/hilled potato bed left, supported soybean row back, lettuce right, one shared reservoir below rear row and supply/drain connections unchanged. Amber storm light outside; grow lights reduced but still operating. The dry service alcove at far edge may show the existing foil-wrapped heat tank with its front flap folded back, no new heating device. One floor-to-ceiling service rail borders the growing zone, separate from the reservoir.
STATE 1: Grown crops and reservoir exposed; no thermal screen or reservoir lid yet.
STATE 2: A simple clean fabric thermal screen hangs from the service rail around the outer sides of the growing area, open at the viewing side so plants and reservoir remain visible. The shared reservoir now has a plain fitted steel cover, preserving the aerating return air gap. No exterior reservoir wrap yet.
STATE 3: The same screen and covered shared reservoir. Foil/felt insulation now wraps the reservoir outside, with all supply, drain and pump connections preserved. No second reservoir, no plants moved.
